title: Public-data provenance and experimental model status

preview.source: EdNet KT1 third-party public viewer preview

model_status.recommendations: Live: deterministic editorial prerequisite ranking; independent skill checks stored locally
model_status.occupational_classification: Existing exploratory trained classifiers, not next-lesson models
model_status.deep_knowledge_tracing: Real mathematics GRU pilot trained and evaluated: 53.63% on 509 held-out next-response predictions vs 59.53% majority-class baseline. Below baseline; not deployed. Full EdNet not acquired.
model_status.gru_mathematics_pilot_data: 52 sequence histories, 2,624 observations; trace-disjoint evaluation (original student IDs unavailable)

sources.label: O*NET 31.0 software skills
sources.detail: 31,821 occupation-to-technology associations; these are examples of workplace tools, not evidence of individual competence.

sources.label: EdNet KT1
sources.detail: Five pseudonymous learner histories in a nonrepresentative preview. Full original archive is not in the repository.

sources.label: ASSISTments 2009–2010 corrected
sources.detail: School mathematics student-problem logs; separate from vocational/technical skills.

sources.label: O*NET 31.0 essential skills
sources.detail: 18,200 occupation-level ratings in official release; archive not downloaded in this integration.

sources.label: O*NET 31.0 transferable skills
sources.detail: 45,500 occupation-level ratings in official release; archive not downloaded in this integration.

notes: The preview is not a random sample and must not be used to report model accuracy.
English and school mathematics responses do not establish student knowledge in Python, AI, cloud, or cybersecurity.
No learner-level dataset is published on the public GitHub Pages site.
Model code in the repository does not imply that full-scale training has been executed.

A small PyTorch GRU on independently sourced mathematics sequence histories was trained and scored. It underperformed the majority-class baseline; do not treat this as a successful recommendation model.
